title: DWG BLOCK_RECORD list validation and scratch reuse
mode: Local source-backed implementation and focused generated round-trip validation
scope: Reduce writer-owned copies on the deferred DWG BLOCK_RECORD emission path.
Replace per-member complete object-map scans and owner-list prefix scans in final list validation.
Preserve legacy sorted handle emission and modern callback-order emission.
Bound the one reusable owner-list validation/sort scratch by the existing per-list count cap.

localChange.summary: emitDeferredBlockControl now borrows modern block/model/paper entity vectors for output, reuses one vector for legacy filtering/sorting and per-list validation, sorts the existing object map before closure validation, and uses lower_bound plus sorted adjacent duplicate detection. Later writeDwgHandles sorting remains in place because structural frames append after closure validation.

scratchBound.scope: one owner list at a time; excludes vector allocator capacity overhead

localChange.wireBehavior: No format fields or handle roles changed. Legacy AC1015-and-earlier lists remain sorted before emission; modern lists retain callback/source order.

results: libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip passed (3.50 s), including the generated version matrix and non-empty block membership paths.
libdxfrw_dwg_block_record_xref_roundtrip passed (0.13 s), covering six DWG versions.

remainingWork: recordBlockOwnedEntity still scans its target vector before each append; evaluate a rollback-safe membership index with explicit aggregate memory accounting.
recordRawBlockOwnedEntity has a related insertion-time membership scan.
Other DWG live/work accounting and the independent DXF writer-copy audit remain open under 7S.
limitations: The algorithmic work reduction was not measured with a timing benchmark; correctness was checked through generated writer/reader round trips.
The object-map vector is sorted before validation and is sorted again after structural frames are appended; the second sort remains the authoritative final handle-map ordering.
The scratch cap limits logical vector elements; allocator capacity/metadata and RSS are not claimed as bounded by the payload calculation.
The source worktree is broadly dirty. No unrelated files were reverted, and no commit was created because repository metadata is read-only in this workspace.
